rationale:
226 contrast_failure work items are parked at 'deferred' and cannot be released. They were parked because contrast_failure has NO REGISTERED VERIFIER, and verifyBeforeComplete resolves via checks.GetVerifier(itemType) — an unregistered type completes UNTOUCHED, writing no _verification key. So promoting the 226 today would mint 226 completions that are ungraded by construction. Confirmed empirically on a sibling type: 14 dark_section_audit items completed post-roll on 2026-08-11, 0 of 14 carry a _verification key, against 9 of 9 for hardcoded_section_colors.

The obvious remedy — write a completion-time verifier — was costed on 2026-08-12 and has NO SURVIVOR. Contrast cannot be settled from source (a CSS var(--x,#fallback) literal is present in the source and never applied), so every option computes contrast by fetching the page, and verifier_coverage_test.go records a STANDING OBJECTION in three places to putting an outbound probe on the completion path (image_url_404, backend_entry_orphaned, asset_reference_404). That objection kills all three forks, not just the browser one: a narrower predicate is narrower in PREDICATE, not in MECHANISM.

So this takes asset_reference_404's posture instead: RETRACT ON THE DISCOVERY PATH. The render audit already re-measures every page weekly with a browser; when it re-measures a page and no longer finds a pairing failing, that is the same information a verifier would fetch, taken where the probe is already precedented. The shared closer already exists (resolveWorkItems, work_items_common.go, same package as the producer, which already holds a tx).

The only thing missing was scope: the audit reported HOW MANY pages it covered, not WHICH, and a repaired page reports NOTHING — so a clean page is indistinguishable from one never visited, and the audited set cannot be derived from the findings. bugs_open/242 shipped the counts on 2026-08-11; this adds the identities.

TWO DECISIONS THE COUNCIL SHOULD RULE ON EXPLICITLY, both stated rather than buried:

(1) 'deferred' IS NOT IN workItemClosedStatuses (which is complete/verified/rejected/wont_fix/cancelled), so this WILL close parked items — the 226 drain as each site's weekly audit confirms a repair, without anyone unparking them. I judge that correct and am not treating it as a side effect: the park exists to prevent UNGRADED completions, and a retraction is the opposite of one — it closes on a fresh positive measurement by the same instrument that filed the row, stamping result.resolved_by and result.reason as the evidence. That is the grading the park was waiting for. It is reported as retracted_parked so the draining is visible rather than silent. If the council disagrees, the contained alternative is one added status in the retraction's NOT IN list.

(2) The handoff this implements specified the still-failing set as 'exactly the keys already computed at write_render_audit_findings_action.go:266'. THAT SPEC IS WRONG AND I DID NOT FOLLOW IT. Line 266 is reached only by findings that survive two filters — the locked-component skip and the max_items cap. A finding whose culprit class lives in a LOCKED component, or which the cap dropped, was MEASURED AND IS STILL FAILING but is not filed. Building the set from the filed items would read 'not filed' as 'fixed' and close those tickets — a false completion, the exact outcome the park of 226 exists to prevent. The set is therefore built from payload.Contrast directly. This is proven by induced fault: mutating the set back to the filed items makes TestWriteRenderAuditFindings_MeasuredButUnfiledFindingsAreNotRetracted fail.

over_image approximations count as STILL-OBSERVED for the same reason. The adapter's own header calls that backdrop unknown; 'I could not tell' is not a positive observation of health, and a pairing that has gone from firm to approximate has not been shown fixed.

OTHER CONSUMERS OF THIS RESPONSE, enumerated rather than asserted (owner ruling 2026-07-29 §3). Live agents referencing render_audit: exactly one, render-audit-agent, whose steps are audit (request_render_audit) and write_findings (write_render_audit_findings) — both in this lane. In Go, the only other reader of the same collected-data field is execute_vision_prompt_action.go, which resolves ONLY .renders via resolveVisionImageRefs to feed the design critic and never reads .summary; a new summary key cannot affect it. Nothing else decodes the response.

MEASURED 2026-08-12 against the live DB, with controls that came out the other way: contrast_failure = 226 rows, 226 deferred, 0 carrying batch_id, max(attempt_count)=0, 0 ever completed — against empty_section 61/61 and hardcoded_section_colors 15/15 carrying a batch_id. That zero is why this change also populates batch_id: resolveWorkItems' self-protection guard is 'batch_id IS DISTINCT FROM $6', and NULL IS DISTINCT FROM <uuid> is TRUE, so the guard has never once been able to fire for this producer. The set logic is the primary defence; the guard is the backstop a destructive operation should not go without.

plan.summary: Teach the render audit to close its own tickets: the adapter reports WHICH pages it successfully measured, and the findings-writer retracts contrast_failure items that are absent from a measured page — asset_reference_404's discovery-path posture, replacing a completion-time verifier that three standing objections refuse.

edits.rationale: Adds the audited-page IDENTITIES alongside bugs_open/242's counts. It must travel in the ADAPTER'S RESPONSE: request_render_audit_action.go already computes a urls_audited metadata value and it is DESTROYED, because an awaiting step's own result never survives the park (persistAwaitingStateWithRetry keeps only awaited-request entries, RFC_012 addendum 2, owner-ruled option B). That is why 242 had to echo its counts through the request into the response rather than fix it at the requester. Appended AFTER the reachability guard so an unreachable page is excluded BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a second condition a later reader can forget to keep in step — 'audited' must mean SUCCESSFULLY MEASURED, never 'requested', which is the rule RenderAuditResult.Unreachable already states for itself. omitempty matches the PagesTotal/Truncated precedent, so version skew degrades to today's behaviour.

The retraction itself, inside the transaction that already files the run's findings. Three conditions must all hold, each because the obvious version is wrong: (1) the item's page is in Summary.PagesAudited — never the pages REQUESTED, since an unreachable page measured nothing; (2) the pairing is absent from what this run OBSERVED, where that set is built from payload.Contrast and NOT from the items this run FILED, because a locked-culprit skip and a max_items drop are both 'still broken, not filed' and closing them would be a false completion; (3) the row is not already settled, applied by resolveWorkItems itself. AllOfType is never set — the wide branch would close every open contrast ticket for the site including pages this run never opened. Also populates batch_id, which makes the closer's 'never close what THIS run just raised' guard operative for the first time (measured: 0 of 226 rows carry one, against 61/61 and 15/15 for types filed through the discovery-check path).

The exemption for contrast_failure stays, but its REASON was unsound and is rewritten. It said 'the dedup key plus the NEXT render audit is the verifier'. That is (a) the argument RFC_017 refuted on 2026-08-08, six days after the line was authored in f2a222964 and never revisited; (b) an inference from ABSENCE, which CheckResult.Resolved's contract forbids in writing — a pairing also stops being re-filed when the page is unreachable or a cap dropped it; and (c) never once exercised: 0 of 226 rows dispatched, completed or re-detected, max(attempt_count)=0. Shipping the fix and keeping the false reason would leave the next reader the same wrong argument. The entry is EDITED rather than removed because no verifier is being registered — the literal_markdown/unbuilt_internal_link precedent of removing the entry applies only when one is. The stale cross-reference in dark_section_audit ('same posture as contrast_failure') is corrected too, without deciding whether that type should be verified — that is bugs_open/213's call or the owner's.
edits.sketch:
-"contrast_failure": {catMechanical, "...the dedup key contrast_failure:<page>#<selector> plus the NEXT render audit is the verifier, and the two-strike rule catches a persistent pairing"},
+"contrast_failure": {catMechanical, "...Deliberately NOT a verifier candidate — verification needs a browser, i.e. an outbound probe on the completion path, the same standing objection as image_url_404, backend_entry_orphaned and asset_reference_404. It does not NEED one: since 2026-08-12 the producer retracts its own findings on a positive re-observation, scoped to the pages the audit successfully measured (summary.pages_audited) and never to the pages it merely requested, stamping result.resolved_by/reason as the evidence"},

edits.rationale: Pins the success-only semantics at the source, where a later edit is most likely to break it: an unreachable page must never enter pages_audited, a page WITH findings must (it was measured), and a REPAIRED page reporting nothing must also be listed — that last is the whole reason the field exists. Also pins the Pages-vs-PagesAudited disagreement, because a future reader who 'tidies' them into agreement removes the guarantee.

Induced-fault proof rather than hope, following check_asset_reference_404's header. Every expectation names the exact item_key of each UPDATE, so a WIDENING of scope breaks ExpectationsWereMet instead of passing quietly. The load-bearing half is the negatives: a retraction that only ever confirms 'the bad pairing is gone' would also close a page that failed to load. All four guards were then proven live by MUTATION — reverting each one to its plausible-but-wrong form makes exactly the corresponding test fail: still-failing-set-from-filed-items, no-audited-page-scope, over_image-counts-as-fixed, and a parked counter that does not discriminate.

grounded_in: verifier_coverage_test.go, the exemption being rewritten, verbatim as it stands today: "minted by write_render_audit_findings (actions pkg, outside this sensor's glob); verification needs a browser — the dedup key contrast_failure:<page>#<selector> plus the NEXT render audit is the verifier, and the two-strike rule catches a persistent pairing" — the claim this change makes true for the first time, having never been exercised (0 of 226 rows dispatched, completed or re-detected).

verifier_coverage_test.go on asset_reference_404, the posture being copied: "Deliberately NOT a verifier candidate — verification would put an outbound HTTP probe in the completion path... It does not NEED one: the check retracts its own findings through CheckResult.Resolved on a positive 2xx/3xx re-observation, which is the same information a verifier would fetch, taken on the discovery path where the probe is already precedented".

render_audit_action.go on RenderAuditResult.Unreachable, which is why the retraction scope is measured-not-requested: "Unreachable pages are reported rather than skipped: a page that will not load is a worse finding than one with poor contrast, and silently dropping it would let a dead page pass as clean".

work_items_common.go on resolveWorkItems' guard, inoperative for this producer until this change populates batch_id: "`batch_id IS DISTINCT FROM $batch` — never close what THIS run just raised. A check that both files and resolves the same key in one run is contradicting itself; without this it would thrash an item open/closed on every sweep and look stable in aggregate".

work_items_common.go on workItemClosedStatuses, the list that decides decision (1): "closed (retraction): complete verified rejected wont_fix cancelled" — 'deferred' is absent, so retraction closes parked items, which is why that consequence is put to the council as a decision rather than shipped as a side effect.

work_items_common.go on resolveWorkItems' wide branch, which this change never uses: "resolve: neither ItemKey nor AllOfType set for item_type %q — set AllOfType explicitly if you really mean every open item of this type for this site".

write_render_audit_findings_action.go, the two filters that make the handoff's 'keys already computed at :266' spec unsafe: findings are dropped at "if htmlCorpusContainsClass(lockedHTML, c.Class) { skippedLocked++; continue }" and then at "if len(toFile) > maxItems { dropped = len(toFile) - maxItems; toFile = toFile[:maxItems] }" — both measured-and-failing, neither filed.

MEASURED 2026-08-12 on clients_db, disconfirmable because the controls came out the other way: contrast_failure = 226 rows / 226 deferred / 0 with batch_id / max(attempt_count)=0 / 0 completed, against empty_section 61 rows / 61 with batch_id / max_attempts 3 / 10 completed and hardcoded_section_colors 15 / 15 / 9.

CONSUMERS ENUMERATED, not asserted (owner ruling 2026-07-29 §3): the only live agent whose config references render_audit is render-audit-agent, steps = ensure_site_record, request_render_audit, write_render_audit_findings, complete_workflow — all in this lane. The only other Go reader of the field is execute_vision_prompt_action.go, which resolves ONLY .renders (resolveVisionImageRefs) and never reads .summary.
plan.risks: The operation is DESTRUCTIVE — it closes work items, including 226 parked ones, so the failure mode of a scoping bug is silent false completion rather than a visible error. Four mitigations, all in the change: scope is the successfully-measured pages only; the still-failing set is built before the locked and cap filters so an unfiled-but-broken pairing cannot be read as fixed; AllOfType is never set; and batch_id is now populated so the closer's self-protection guard is operative for the first time. Version skew degrades to INERT: against an un-rolled browser-runner-adapter there is no pages_audited, so nothing is even selected, and the result says retraction_unavailable rather than reporting a bare zero that reads like 'nothing needed closing'. Two services must roll for any behaviour at all — agent-chassis (producer) and browser-runner-adapter (adapter) — and the stamp must be checked PER SERVICE (bugs_open/249). The unaddressed residue is that 226 remains a FLOOR, not a census: the render audit was capped at 25 pages until v1.0.1288, so sites may hold contrast failures that were never filed, and this change closes tickets but does not discover missing ones.
